title: Role-Aware Differential Authorization Testing
goal: Detect more authorization vulnerabilities by comparing the same discovered routes, objects, and actions across multiple approved roles and sessions while preserving evidence-first traceability.
scope: Authenticated web/API testing services, runner parameters, evidence normalization, finding generation, and tests for role-differential authorization behavior.
generation_reason: The operator asked what should happen next in an AI-first evidence-first pentest system to discover more vulnerabilities. Role-aware differential testing is a high-value next step for IDOR, broken access control, privilege escalation, and tenant boundary findings.

review_findings: More vulnerabilities require authenticated role comparison, not only single-session scanning.
Existing authenticated scanning and run credential vault work provide a safe foundation.
Evidence-first output must compare responses and actions without leaking secrets.

inputs.prerequisite_backlog: REQUIRES: backlog-351 authenticated web scanning chain and existing credential protection lanes

constraints.active_task_gate: Do not implement until this package is the single active task in NEXT_TASK.md.
constraints.scope_creep_guard: Focus on differential authorization evidence across approved accounts and sessions. Do not build a general exploit framework or bypass approval gates.
constraints.credential_safety: Use existing protected secret references and runtime binding. Do not persist plaintext credentials or response bodies containing secret material.

success_criteria: The system can test the same route/object/action as anonymous, low-privilege, peer-user, and higher-privilege roles when those approved contexts exist.
Response comparisons capture status code, redirect behavior, stable content fingerprints, object ownership signals, and write-action outcomes without storing raw secrets.
Findings distinguish horizontal IDOR, vertical privilege escalation, anonymous access leakage, and tenant boundary issues.
Evidence artifacts include both allowed and denied control observations so findings are reproducible.
AI-loop or planner output can propose role-differential tests only when prerequisite sessions and scope are present.

acceptance_criteria: Tests prove a peer-user object access is detected as horizontal authorization risk.
Tests prove admin-only or high-privilege action access by a lower role is detected as vertical authorization risk.
Tests prove missing role/session prerequisites produce a coverage gap rather than a false pass.
No approval, scope/ROE, credential, runtime binding, or kill-switch bypass occurs.

before_promotion: NEXT_TASK.md must contain this task as the single active task.
after_completion: Promote the next true open task into NEXT_TASK.md, or record that no active backlog task remains in NEXT_TASK.md.

out_of_scope: Credential stuffing, password spraying, or brute force.
Bypassing scope/ROE, approval gates, runtime binding, or kill-switch behavior.
